questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a good university in an english speaking country. I chose UT Austin because the city seemed nice, Texas sounded fun and the weather is really good.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would be a 10 if it wasnt so expensive

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They hosted a bunch of events before the semester started. Those events were great for meeting other international students and exchange students but also for getting the information you needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a little hard but that was because i started late. Start early and it will be fine i think. I recommend looking into the co-ops as they looked great to live in. They might be a little dirty and some of them host a lot of parties, but they are very affordable and a great place to socialize.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You pretty much have to live in the West Campus area. It is where everyone lives and all the fun stuff happens so it is 100% worth the extra cost.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got to register late so a lot of the classes were already full. A lot of the other exchange students got to skip the waitlists by asking their advisor but some, including me,  did not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We got assigned and academic advisor who was supposed to help us some were good some were not.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a lot of backup plans ready

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I ended up with the two hardest undergraduate physics classes in all of UT so mine were pretty rough

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They leave a lot of it up to you. One of my classes did not follow a book, did not post lecture notes and did not give any practice problems. Theres also a lot of tests and homework

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PHY 375R Introduction to relativity. PHY336L Fluid dynamics. PHY341 Pseudoscience. MAN 320 Foundations of management. PED 104P beginning tennis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take a PED class in any sport you like! They are fun and a great way to meet people from a bunch of different majors

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The trips i went on

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a club for any kind of interests you might have

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Buy "The big ticket" it is a 200$ ticket that gives you free access to all the sports events all year. Go to the football games and go to the tailgates.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of Texas. Go to louisiana or colorado. Go on a roadtrip (or several).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to all the events you can and honestly just talk to everyone. Go to Cain and Ables on Tuesdays for their dollar beer night.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How social and talkative people are

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Dont focus too much on the schoolwork - the classes are hard to fail. Try not to just talk with other danes as your semester will be so much more fun if you make local/international friends. Go on trips.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a pool on campus for when you want to cool down. (it will be around degrees until late september / early october)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people i met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing school, fun, and relaxing. There is always a million things to do so you can easily get FOMO

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
